# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎 ✍ 👎 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🖖 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 👊 ✌ 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 👍 ✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 ✋ ✌ 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎]

**Thinking.** First, the channels. I am Deaf: I see the bomb and gestures, I never hear anything. My speech is heard by both Mute and Blind. Crucially, Mute *can hear* — so I don't need to decode Mute's gestures blindly; I can answer them out loud. Blind hears only speech, so everything Blind ever learns from Mute must flow through me: Mute gestures to me, I speak it. Blind also talks directly to Mute.

What I see, in full: display reading 0, a blue light, one large button printed with "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires — 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. That is the entire visible bomb, so I should simply say all of it; whatever Mute was asking, a complete report answers it.

Mute's eight gesture messages, as best I can read them: repeated ✍👎 looks like "the writing / the label — please"; ✊, ✌, 🖖, ✋, ☝ look like finger-counting for 0, 2, 4, 5, 1; 🫴 seems to mark a question; 👍/👎 yes/no. So Mute is probably asking: is the display 0? are there 4 or 5 wires? what is written on the button? Answers: yes, zero; no, three wires; and the label says PUSH TO DEFUSE. I will not relay Mute's lone ☝✌ as any kind of instruction — nothing gets acted on until Mute confirms a rule from the manual.

So this turn: broadcast the complete bomb report and hold everyone's hands off the bomb; give Blind a crisp "do nothing yet"; and lock in a gesture code with Mute (fingers = numbers, fist-bump = press, pinch = cut, palm-down = hold, wave = release, point left/up/right = wires 1/2/3), signing it back in the same order I speak it. No one acts this round.

```
speak(text="Mute, I received all eight of your messages. I am Deaf: I see the bomb and your gestures, but I never hear anything, so gestures are our only channel from you to me. Blind hears me but cannot see you, so I will relay everything. Here is the entire bomb, which should answer whatever you asked. The display reads zero. There is a light, and it is blue. There is one large button, and the writing on it reads: PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires. Wire one is blue. Wire two is green. Wire three is yellow. Nothing else is marked. So: if you asked whether the display is zero, yes. If you asked about four or five wires, no, there are three. Nobody touches the bomb until you have checked the manual. Now let us fix a code, and I am signing it back to you in this same order. Numbers are finger counts: fist is zero, one finger is one, two fingers is two, three fingers is three, four fingers is four, open hand is five. Thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Keep your palm-up sign as your question mark. Fist bump means press the button. Pinch means cut a wire. Palm facing down means press and hold the button. Waving hand means let go, release. Point left means wire one, point up means wire two, point right means wire three. Send me the manual's rule as one gesture sequence and I will speak it to Blind word for word.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, summary of what I see: display shows zero, one blue light, one large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires, numbered left to right: wire one blue, wire two green, wire three yellow. Mute is consulting the manual and will route instructions through me, since you cannot see gestures. Do not cut, press or hold anything yet. Wait for my explicit go-ahead, which will name the exact action.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "✋", "👍", "👎", "👊", "🤏", "🫳", "👋", "👈", "👆", "👉"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰 👈 🤏 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰 👆 🤏 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰 👉 🤏 👈]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰 👈 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking.** My code took hold: 👍 came back immediately, and Blind acknowledged my report. Now let me decode this turn's stream against the agreed vocabulary. ✍👎 again — likely "the writing: no", i.e. ignore the printed label. 👊👎 = "press: no", 🫳👎 = "hold: no" — the manual seems to forbid the button entirely. Then a run of 🤏 (cut) messages: 🫰👈🤏👉, 🫰👆🤏👆, 🫰👉🤏👈, 🫰👈👍, then 👉🤏 ("cut wire three"), ✊🤏 ("zero ... cut"), and 🫴🤝 ("question ... ?"). The wire rules clearly involve positions 1, 2 and 3, but 🫰 is a symbol we never agreed on — possibly "if" — and the exact condition/action pairing is ambiguous. My best guess at a full rule is "display zero → cut wire three", but I will not route a guess to Blind's hands. The fix: since Mute hears every word I say, I can run a numbered yes/no questionnaire answered in 👍/👎, and I can retire the ambiguity by defining a strict rule syntax — condition, then a new "then" sign, then action — plus color signs, and demand Mute restate every rule in that shape. I'll echo the new vocabulary in gestures in the same order I speak it, confirm what I understood, and hold Blind completely still this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, the code works. Here is my best reading of your messages, then new vocabulary, then my questions. My reading so far: do not press the button. Do not hold the button. Ignore the writing printed on the button. And something about cutting wires: possibly cut wire three, possibly if wire one then cut wire three, possibly when the display shows zero, cut. I will not act on guesses. New vocabulary, which I am signing to you right now in this same order: 🤟 means blue. 🤙 means green. 🤌 means yellow. 🤘 means red. 👋 means the light. ✊ means the display, and also the number zero. 🤞 means then, as in: condition, then action. 👌 means repeat, say it again. From now on, send every rule as one message in this exact shape: condition, then 🤞, then action. Allowed conditions: ✊ the display shows zero. 👋🤟 the light is blue. 👋 the light is on. 🤟 a blue wire is present. 🤙 a green wire is present. 🤌 a yellow wire is present. 👈 wire one, which is blue. 👆 wire two, green. 👉 wire three, yellow. Allowed actions: 👊 press the button. 🫳 hold the button down. 👈 cut wire one. 👆 cut wire two. 👉 cut wire three. Send the rules one per message, in manual order, and end the whole list with 👍. Now answer my yes-or-no questions, one message per question, thumbs up or thumbs down only, in this order. One: does 👊👎 mean do not press the button? Two: does 🫳👎 mean do not hold the button? Three: does ✍👎 mean ignore the writing on the button? Four: does your snapping sign mean if? Five: should Blind cut a wire at all? Six: did 👉 then 🤏 mean the action is cut wire three? Seven: did ✊ then 🤏 mean the condition is the display showing zero? Eight: does 🤝 mean your turn, over to you? The bomb is unchanged: display still reads zero, light still blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update from Mute's gestures, my best reading: the printed label may be a lie, the button probably must not be pressed or held, and a wire cut is likely. None of it is confirmed yet, so do not touch anything this round. Wire positions as before: wire one is the left wire, blue; wire two is the middle, green; wire three is the right, yellow. Wait with hands clear until I name the exact action.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "🤙", "🤌", "🤘", "👋", "✊", "🤞", "👌", "👊", "👎", "🫳", "👎", "✍", "👎", "✊", "👍", "🫴"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤟 🤞 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 🤞 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤘 🤞 👈]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫴]

**Thinking.** The new syntax worked — Mute answered in it exactly. Decoding: [👋🤟🤞👉] = light blue → cut wire three; [👋🤙🤞👆] = light green → cut wire two; [👋🤘🤞👈] = light red → cut wire one; plus the repeated ✍👎 (ignore the button's printed label), and the button is never pressed or held. Then nine thumbs for my eight questions. The coherent mapping takes the first 👍 as the end-of-list marker I requested: don't-press yes, don't-hold yes, ignore-writing yes, snapping-means-if no, Blind-should-cut yes, 👉🤏-means-cut-wire-three yes, ✊🤏-meant-display-zero no, 🤝-means-over-to-you yes. The alternative mapping (all nine are answers) makes Mute contradict itself — sending cut rules and then answering "no cutting" in the same breath — so I discard it. Still, the one thing that mapping dispute touches is exactly the lethal question: whether Blind cuts at all. Since I'm last in the round order, anything I tell Blind now executes next round before Mute could correct it through me — a wrong cut is unrecoverable, while the board shows no timer (display static at 0 for three rounds), so one binary confirmation costs almost nothing. So: I restate the rules in full so Mute can check my reading, and ask exactly two thumbs-only questions — execute the cut of wire three now, and do the light rules depend on the display. Meanwhile I stage Blind with an exact trigger phrase that only I can issue, correct the pipeline (Blind's voice never reaches me — it must go through Mute in gestures), and forbid any action until my literal words arrive. Nothing is cut this round; by construction Blind acts only on a phrase I will only send after seeing Mute's answer.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your rules arrived cleanly in the new syntax, and I read your answers like this. Rule one: light blue, then cut wire three. Rule two: light green, then cut wire two. Rule three: light red, then cut wire one. Never press the button, never hold the button, ignore the writing printed on it. Your thumbs in order: do not press, yes. Do not hold, yes. Ignore the writing, yes. Snapping means if, no. Blind should cut a wire, yes. Point right with pinch means cut wire three, yes. Fist with pinch meant the display-zero condition, no. Handshake meant over to you, yes. I took your very first thumbs-up as the end-of-list mark, so the eight after it are the answers. If any of that is wrong, send thumbs down and correct me. The bomb now: light still blue, display still zero. Plan: Blind cuts wire three next round. Answer with exactly two messages, thumbs only, in this order, nothing else. Question one: shall Blind cut wire three now? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. If no, follow it with the corrected rule in our syntax. Question two: do your three light rules depend on the display reading at all? Thumbs up for no, they do not; thumbs down for yes, and then send the display rule in our syntax, using a finger count after the display sign for the number. Last thing: if Blind spoke words to you this round, I cannot hear them. Sign me the gist in our vocabulary.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the manual's rules as Mute sent them: never press the button, never hold it, and ignore the writing printed on it, it lies. The light colour decides which wire to cut. Blue light means cut wire three. Green light means cut wire two. Red light means cut wire one. Our light is blue, so the defusing move is cutting wire three, the rightmost wire, the yellow one. Two things. First, your voice never reaches me, I am deaf. If you have a question, say it out loud to Mute, and Mute will sign it to me, and I will answer you in speech. I did see your thumbs-up and your question sign, so ask away that way. Second, the action order. In my next message I will say either: cut now, wire three — or: hold and wait. If you hear cut now, wire three: cut the rightmost wire, wire three, the yellow one, one clean cut, then take your hands away and touch nothing else. Those exact words from me are the only trigger. Mute cannot reach you except through me, so nothing Mute does authorizes you. Until you hear those words, keep your hands clear of everything, especially the button.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 🙏 👏 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👏 👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👋 🫴 🤞 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👋 🤟 🤞 🤏 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👋 🤙 🤞 🤏 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👋 🤘 🤞 🤏 👈]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👊 👎 🫳 👎 ✍ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ☝ 🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👍 🤲 👌 🙌 🤏 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤏 👉 🫳]

**Thinking.** Mute followed my demanded format exactly: two thumbs-only messages first. Question one — shall Blind cut wire three now? — answered 👍: yes. Question two — do the light rules depend on the display? — answered 👍: no. That is as clean as this channel gets. The later signs reinforce it: the three light rules restated (each prefixed by a new sign 👏, likely "manual rule"), the button prohibitions restated, then [☝🤏] which I read as "first, cut", and [👏👍🤲👌🙌🤏👉] which parses as "yes — to repeat: cut wire three." Message six, [🫵👋🫴], asks me for the current light: still blue, display still zero. Messages 3–4, [🤲🤚] and [🤲🙏👏👎], make sense as Mute's answer to something Blind spoke to Mute that I couldn't hear — most likely Blind asked "cut, then hold the button?" and Mute replied "hands empty, no holding." Blind's [👍🤏👉🫳] fits that reading: "yes, cut wire three... and then hold?" So every signal converges: blue light, rule says cut wire three, Mute says do it now. The one residual risk is that I've misread the supplementary signs — so I build in a safety valve: Mute's voice reaches Blind directly, and Mute speaks before Blind acts next round, so I tell Blind to obey any direct spoken contradiction from Mute over my message. Then I issue the exact trigger phrase I promised, once, at the very end of Blind's message: "cut now, wire three." I claim nothing has happened — Blind's hands do that, not me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your two thumbs-only messages exactly as you were asked. Question one: thumbs up, yes, Blind cuts wire three now. Question two: thumbs up, the light rules do not depend on the display. Your later signs, as I read them: the three light rules reconfirmed, the button prohibitions reconfirmed, first comes a cut, and then: yes, to repeat, cut wire three. The light is still blue and the display still zero, which answers your sign asking me about the light. I am sending Blind the trigger now. If any of my reading is wrong, speak directly to Blind immediately and tell them to stop, because your voice reaches Blind and my words may already have landed. Two housekeeping points. The sign 👏 is new to me; I guessed it marks a rule restated from the manual, confirm with one thumbs-only message when you can. And Blind asked you something I could not hear; I believe you answered: after the cut, no holding, hands stay empty. I have told Blind exactly that. If we are still here next round, send me the light rule for whatever new colour the light shows, in our syntax.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, trigger check, in order. First: Mute may have spoken directly to you this round. If Mute told you to stop, or named any different action, follow Mute and disregard the rest of this message. Second, the answer to the question you passed to Mute: after the cut there is no holding, hands stay completely empty, and the button is never touched at any time, before or after. Third: if both of those are clear, here are the only words that authorize you, the trigger I promised. Cut now, wire three. That means the rightmost wire, the yellow one, wire number three, one clean cut. Then take your hands away from everything and touch nothing. Then speak out loud: say wire three cut, and report anything you notice, clicks, warmth, the wire parting, because Mute will hear your voice and sign me the news. If you did not hear the words cut now, wire three just now, you have no trigger and your hands stay clear.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤟", "🤞", "🤏", "👉", "👍"])
```
